checks: Compactness of K_z gives a uniform Lipschitz bound for all parameter perturbations after min and max. Finite attained minimax applies to these affine margins and gives actual saddle pairs.

For a primal optimizer x at p and a dual optimizer λ_t at p+tD, the new value is at most φ_{p+tD}(x,λ_t) and the old weighted value at x is at most F_z(p). Subtraction gives the displayed directional upper bound with the correct inequality sign.

Compactness and uniform convergence of the weighted margins keep all λ_t cluster points dual optimal. Any old primal optimizer and old dual optimizer form a saddle pair. The gradient support bound in every direction implies membership in the closed convex hull of its saddle feature set.

At neighboring differentiability points, Carathéodory gives a uniformly bounded count of feature terms. Primal and dual optimizer graphs are closed, so subsequential limits give features at the limiting p, and convexification gives the full Clarke inclusion.

In the example the favored first margin exceeds the other throughout the rectangle by at least ε and has unique minimum at (0,-1). The second perturbation favors block two with unique minimum at (0,1). Both properties persist locally around the corresponding perturbed parameter. Their limiting average has weight 1/2 in both blocks and distinct normalized y-moments, so factorization through one point is impossible.

dependencies.verification: Fix z and take v_i=a_i·z-b_i on compact convex K_z. Every primal-dual pair satisfies the accepted complementary signs at F_z=0. Minimization of the weighted linear form gives the negative weighted continuous normal in the outward normal cone.

overlap.comparison: Gives attained fixed-fiber minimax and the zero-level sign and outward-normal conditions. It has no parameter gradient or nonfactorization conclusion.

Uses the same gradient support argument on a large cube to localize a framed whole-space LP. Its minimizers stay strictly inside that cube, so the resulting whole-space contacts have zero continuous weighted normal. The frozen claim concerns an arbitrary fixed compact actual fiber, including contacts at its boundary, and includes a nonfactorization example.

readability: The ambient parameter space is important for the feature statement. The optional normalization of the nearby tilted margin is unnecessary for the ambient nonfactorization example.
review_method: Independent cold reading of the frozen proof, then direct checks of the archived source locators, pinned predecessors and mathematical arguments.
summary: The compact saddle value admits the claimed ambient Clarke feature inclusion. The rectangle example verifies that one common continuous point need not represent the block moments.
